intended_object: Given a linear representation ρ : G → Aut_R(M) of a monoid on an R-module M of homogeneous coordinates, the induced action of G on the points of the projective scheme Proj(Sym_R M). Here g acts through the scheme automorphism obtained by pulling back along Sym(ρ(g)⁻¹). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (Milne, Algebraic Groups §7).
explanation:
`symmetricAlgebraMapIso R e`, for `e : M ≃ N`, is the isomorphism Proj(Sym N) ≅ Proj(Sym M) given by `Proj.map` of the graded map Sym(e). It is contravariant: `symmetricAlgebraMapIso_trans` shows that it reverses composition. So g acts through `(symmetricAlgebraMapIso R (ρ g).symm).hom`, and the inverse makes this a left action; the `one_smul` and `mul_smul` proofs compile.

I checked that this matches the geometric convention. Take M = V^∨ with the contragredient representation. A homogeneous prime q is sent to Sym(ρ(g)⁻¹)⁻¹(q) = Sym(ρ(g))(q). The ideal of the point g·[v] is {f : ρ(g⁻¹)f ∈ p_v} = ρ(g)(p_v), so the two agree.

The generality is natural: an arbitrary monoid G, a commutative ring R, and a module M with no finiteness or freeness assumptions. The construction is specific to symmetric algebras and linear representations, which is exactly what it is meant to be. Mathlib has no actions on Proj induced by linear representations, so there is no more general counterpart. Packaging this as a `MulAction` on the underlying points, which the docstring says is meant to be installed as a local instance, is a reasonable formalization.
